committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects federal agencies including the FDA, HHS, and DOD, as well as pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare stakeholders involved in essential medicine supply chains.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary, in coordination with the heads of other relevant Federal departments and agencies and in consultation with, as appropriate, stakeholders who have relevant expertise

dimensions.assessment: Imposes mandatory reporting, risk assessment, and supply chain mapping duties on federal agencies, and requires regular reporting on medicines sourced from China by the DOD.
dimensions.evidence: conduct a comprehensive risk assessment of the supply chains for active pharmaceutical ingredients and drugs included on the Essential Medicines List

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs for federal agencies to conduct risk assessments, map supply chains, and produce multiple recurring reports for Congress, though specific funding amounts are not stated.
Creates new ongoing statutory duties for federal agencies to coordinate, map, monitor, and report on pharmaceutical supply chains and essential medicines.
dimensions.evidence: map, or otherwise visualize, the supply chains, from manufacturing of key starting materials through manufacturing of finished dosage forms and distribution

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent or recurring ongoing duties, such as biennial updates to the essential medicine list and annual or semi-annual reports to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: not less frequently than every 2 years

missing_information: Specific figures on federal appropriations or costs required to implement the supply chain mapping and reporting systems.
importance_detail.rationale: The MAPS Act establishes federal requirements for the FDA, HHS, and DOD to maintain essential medicine lists, conduct supply chain risk assessments, map supply chains, and submit recurring reports to Congress. It directly affects federal agencies, pharmaceutical supply chains, and military procurement reporting.
